name: Ultimate Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: A belt made for one match. Its sponsor's own explanation, read out in the ring on the second Summit's last night, was that the two men it had been made for were the only two in e-wrestling who had held major titles in two separate federations at the same time — and that both had since lost those belts, which did not diminish what they had done. Four federation presidents sat at a table at ringside and let the match stand. It is the only championship the Summit ever held of its own, and no defence of it survives anywhere in the held record.
notes: Introduced and explained in the ring by its own sponsor on the second Summit's fourth night, 30 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/the-summit-of-e-wrestling-day-4-1991-12-30.html): "This is not a title that can be taken away by normal means. This title denotes supremacy in the ring, which is something only time can efface." Sponsored by TNT Enterprises and sanctioned, per that speech, under the aegis of the four e-federation presidents seated at ringside. Contested once in the surviving record and never defended in it.

name: The Road Warrior's Cup
epitaph: The Summit's own tag-team tournament: sixteen teams at the first Summit in Montreal in July 1991, won by the Soviets, and the seventh Summit's in June 1995, won by Death Warmed Over.

name: The Summit Royal Rumble
epitaph: The Summit's own Royal Rumble, won twice in 1991: by Fury, thirty men over the top rope in Buffalo in July, and by Klingon Phaser, from the fortieth entry of forty, that December.

name: The Von Erich/Freebird Memorial Trophy
epitaph: A six-man tag tournament of fourteen trios, run once, on the second Summit's third night, 29 December 1991. The Big Three won it in four matches in the one night.
